experiences.name: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim
experiences.description: Explore one of the Algarve's most stunning beaches, known for its dramatic limestone cliffs, sea caves, and crystal-clear turquoise waters. Hike the clifftop trail from Benagil and descend to the secluded cove for a refreshing swim.

experiences.name: Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour
experiences.description: Paddle through the iconic Benagil Cave, one of the world's most beautiful sea caves, accessible only by water. A guided kayak tour takes you through hidden grottos and arches along the golden coastline, offering a unique perspective of the Algarve's dramatic geology.

experiences.name: Algarve Wine & Cataplana Tasting Experience
experiences.description: Visit a local winery in the Lagoa wine region, the heart of Algarve viticulture, for a guided tasting of regional wines including Arinto and Negra Mole varieties. Pair your wines with a traditional Cataplana seafood stew prepared by a local chef.

experiences.name: Ria Formosa Natural Park Boat Tour
experiences.description: Cruise through the stunning Ria Formosa lagoon system, a protected natural park spanning 60km of coastline. Discover barrier islands, flamingo colonies, and secluded barrier beaches only accessible by boat, with stops for swimming and snorkeling in calm lagoon waters.

experiences.name: Silves Castle & Old Town Food Walk
experiences.description: Explore the Moorish red sandstone castle of Silves, the ancient Algarve capital, followed by a guided food walk through the historic old town. Sample local specialties including carob products, medronho brandy, almond sweets, and fresh orange juice at traditional market stalls.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Portugal Algarve
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Faro Airport at 22:30. Take the budget-friendly Eva Bus or Rede Expressos coach from Faro Airport to Lagos (approx. €5-7, ~1.5 hours). Check in to Boutique Taghostel on Rua Dr. Faria e Silva. Grab a late-night snack near the hostel and get settled.

meals.breakfast: N/A - In transit
meals.lunch: N/A - In transit
meals.dinner: Late-night snack: grab a bifana (pork sandwich) or pastel de nata from a 24-hour bakery or convenience store near Lagos bus station (~€2-3)

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book the Faro to Lagos bus ticket online to save time. The hostel is a short walk or cheap taxi (~€5) from Lagos bus station. Keep luggage light for easy transport. Confirm hostel late check-in policy in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recover from travel. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the hostel or a nearby café. Explore the charming historic center of Lagos on foot — visit the Igreja de Santo António (free exterior, small fee inside ~€2), the old city walls, and Praça Gil Eanes. Pick up a local SIM card or map from a nearby shop.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk down to Meia Praia, Lagos's longest and most accessible beach (free entry, ~15-min walk from hostel). Relax on the golden sands, swim in the Atlantic, and soak up the September sun. Rent a beach umbrella and chair if needed (~€5-8 for the set).
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Lagos marina at sunset. Explore the lively Rua 25 de Abril for budget tapas bars and cervejarias. Enjoy a glass of local Algarve wine with petiscos (Portuguese tapas).

meals.breakfast: Café Ginginha or a local pastelaria near the hostel — coffee + pastel de nata (~€2)
meals.lunch: Picnic on the beach: grab fresh bread, local cheese, cured meats, and fruit from Mercado de Lagos or a mini-market (~€5-6)
meals.dinner: O Camilo or a local tasca on Rua 25 de Abril — prato do dia (dish of the day) with soup, main, and drink (~€8-10)

day_by_day.notes: September weather in the Algarve is typically warm (24-28°C) with calm seas — ideal beach conditions. Bring sunscreen and a reusable water bottle. The historic center is very walkable from the hostel.

day_by_day.morning: Take a short local bus or walk (~20 min) to Praia Dona Ana, one of Lagos's most iconic beaches with dramatic golden cliffs and sea stacks. Arrive early to secure a good spot. Explore the rock formations and sea caves along the cliff path.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the coastal cliff path from Praia Dona Ana toward Praia do Camilo (~10-min walk). Praia do Camilo is a smaller, more secluded beach accessible via a wooden staircase — stunning scenery. Continue the cliff walk toward Ponta da Piedade, the most spectacular rock formation in the Algarve (free, ~30-min walk from Camilo). Bring water and snacks.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos town center. Visit the Mercado de Escravos (Slave Market Museum, ~€3) if still open, or browse the local artisan shops. Head to a local wine bar for a tasting of Algarve wines — look for Adega do Cantor or similar local producers.

meals.breakfast: Hostel breakfast if included, or a local café — toast with butter and jam + coffee (~€3)
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic or grab a sandwich from a local padaria (bakery) before heading to the beach (~€4-5)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Adega da Marina near the marina — grilled fish or cataplana (seafood stew) at budget prices (~€10-12)

day_by_day.notes: The cliff walk from Dona Ana to Ponta da Piedade is approximately 3km one way — wear comfortable shoes. The views are absolutely breathtaking and completely free. Sunset at Ponta da Piedade is magical — time your walk accordingly.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Sagres (westernmost point of continental Europe). Take the Eva Bus from Lagos to Sagres (~€4.50 each way, ~1 hour). Visit the impressive Fortaleza de Sagres (€3 entry) — a 15th-century fortress with dramatic ocean views and a giant wind compass (Rosa dos Ventos).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Cabo de São Vicente (~6km from Sagres, or take a taxi ~€8 one way) — the most southwestern point of continental Europe. The lighthouse and cliffs are awe-inspiring. Watch the Atlantic waves crash against the 75-meter cliffs. Browse the small market stalls selling local honey, dried figs, and handicrafts.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Sagres for sunset at the fortress or cliffs, then catch the evening bus back to Lagos. Relax at the hostel common area and meet fellow travelers.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at the hostel or grab a pastel de nata at Lagos bus station before departure (~€2)
meals.lunch: A Sagres — Restaurante Mum's or a local café in Sagres village — fresh grilled fish sandwich or soup (~€6-8)
meals.dinner: Back in Lagos — Tasca do Zé or similar local tasca — bacalhau (salt cod) dish with house wine (~€9-11)

day_by_day.notes: Check the Eva Bus schedule in advance as services to Sagres can be infrequent. The last bus back to Lagos is usually around 19:00-20:00 — confirm times locally. Bring a light jacket as Cabo de São Vicente can be windy even in September.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Praia da Luz, a beautiful village beach about 6km west of Lagos. Take the local bus (Line 1, ~€1.50) or rent a bicycle from a Lagos bike shop (~€10-12/day). The beach is wide, calm, and less crowded than Lagos town beaches. Swim and relax.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cycle or bus back toward Lagos and stop at Praia do Porto de Mós — a large, relatively uncrowded beach with golden cliffs. Explore the rock pools at low tide. Walk the short cliff path for panoramic views.
day_by_day.evening: Saturday evening in Lagos — the town comes alive. Walk through the old town and enjoy the street atmosphere. Visit a local wine shop (garrafeira) and pick up a bottle of Algarve or Alentejo wine (~€5-8) to enjoy at the hostel terrace with new friends.

meals.breakfast: Café Central or similar in Lagos old town — galão (milky coffee) + tosta mista (toasted ham and cheese sandwich) (~€3.50)
meals.lunch: Beach snack bar at Praia da Luz — prego no pão (steak sandwich) or salad (~€7-8)
meals.dinner: Mercado de Lagos food market (if open Saturday evening) or Rua 25 de Abril — grilled chicken piri-piri with fries (~€8-10)

day_by_day.notes: Renting a bicycle is a great budget-friendly way to explore the coastline west of Lagos. The terrain is mostly flat along the coast. Saturday evenings in Lagos are lively — the old town pedestrian streets are perfect for a leisurely evening stroll.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Lagos Sunday market (Mercado Municipal) for fresh local produce, cheeses, olives, and regional products — great for budget shopping and cultural immersion. Stock up on snacks and picnic supplies for the week.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a self-guided kayak or SUP (stand-up paddleboard) rental along the Lagos coastline to explore the sea caves and grottos near Ponta da Piedade from the water. Several operators near the marina offer rentals (~€15-20 for 2 hours) — this is more affordable than guided tours (~€35+). Paddle through the famous golden arches and hidden caves.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset walk along the Lagos seafront promenade (Avenida dos Descobrimentos). Find a bench with a view and enjoy your market purchases with a local beer or wine. Early evening — visit a fado bar or live music venue in the old town for authentic Portuguese culture (many are free entry).

meals.breakfast: Market breakfast — fresh fruit, local bread, and a coffee from a market stall (~€3-4)
meals.lunch: Picnic with market purchases at a scenic cliff-top spot near Ponta da Piedade (~€5-6 total)
meals.dinner: Restaurante O Galeão in Lagos old town — Sunday roast-style Portuguese meal or arroz de marisco (seafood rice) (~€10-12)

day_by_day.notes: For the kayak/SUP rental, book early in the morning as September weekends can still be busy. Always check sea conditions before paddling — the staff at rental shops will advise. The sea caves are best explored at low tide.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip east along the Algarve coast to Portimão and Praia da Rocha. Take the train from Lagos to Portimão (~€2.50, 20 minutes — one of the cheapest and most scenic rail routes in Portugal). Walk from Portimão station to Praia da Rocha (~15 min) — a wide, dramatic beach backed by red sandstone cliffs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Praia da Rocha and the clifftop promenade. Visit the Fortaleza de Santa Catarina (free entry) at the eastern end of the beach for panoramic views over the Arade River estuary. Walk back into Portimão town center and browse the riverside fish market area.
day_by_day.evening: Before returning to Lagos, stop at a Portimão sardine restaurant — Portimão is famous for its grilled sardines (sardinhas assadas). The riverside area has several budget-friendly options. Catch the evening train back to Lagos.

meals.breakfast: Hostel or quick café near Lagos train station — coffee + croissant (~€2.50)
meals.lunch: Beach snack bar at Praia da Rocha — fresh grilled fish or salad (~€8-9)
meals.dinner: Portimão riverside — grilled sardines with bread, salad, and a glass of local wine (~€8-10) before catching the train back

day_by_day.notes: The Lagos-Portimão train runs regularly throughout the day. Check the CP (Comboios de Portugal) website for timetables. Portimão is also known for its Formula 1 circuit — the Autódromo Internacional do Algarve is nearby if that interests you, though tours cost extra.

day_by_day.morning: Wine tasting day! Take the train or bus to Lagoa (~€3, 30 min from Lagos) — the wine capital of the Algarve. Visit Adega Cooperativa do Algarve or Quinta dos Vales winery. Many Algarve wineries offer free or low-cost tastings (~€5-10) with advance booking. Taste local Algarve varietals including Negra Mole and Crato Branco.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue wine exploration — visit a second winery or wine shop in Lagoa. Alternatively, take a short bus to Carvoeiro (~€2), a picturesque fishing village with a small beach and dramatic cliff scenery. Walk the Algar Seco boardwalk (free) — a stunning coastal rock formation with natural pools.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos by bus or train. Visit a local wine bar in Lagos old town to compare Algarve wines with Alentejo and Douro varieties. Many wine bars offer tasting flights for ~€8-12.

meals.breakfast: Lagos café — full Portuguese breakfast (eggs, toast, ham, coffee) (~€4-5)
meals.lunch: Lagoa town center — a local tasca near the winery — prato do dia with local wine pairing (~€9-10)
meals.dinner: Lagos old town wine bar — cheese and charcuterie board with a glass of Algarve wine (~€10-12)

day_by_day.notes: Call ahead to book winery visits — even budget wineries appreciate advance notice. Quinta dos Vales near Lagoa is particularly visitor-friendly and offers affordable tastings. Designate a 'driver' if cycling — or simply use public transport for the wine day.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the western Algarve's wild coast — take the bus to Aljezur (~€4, 1 hour from Lagos). Aljezur is a charming hilltop village with a Moorish castle (free entry) offering panoramic views. Walk up to the castle ruins and explore the old Moorish quarter.
day_by_day.afternoon: From Aljezur, take a local taxi or walk (~4km) to Praia da Arrifana — one of the most dramatic and beautiful beaches in the Algarve, set in a natural amphitheater of cliffs. This is a popular surf beach — watch the surfers or try a beginner surf lesson (~€25-30 including board rental). The beach is part of the Costa Vicentina Natural Park.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Aljezur for the evening bus back to Lagos. Stop at a local café in Aljezur for a medronho (local arbutus berry spirit) tasting — a traditional Algarve experience. Arrive back in Lagos for a relaxed evening.

meals.breakfast: Hostel or Lagos café before departure (~€2-3)
meals.lunch: Beach snack bar at Praia da Arrifana — fresh fish soup and bread (~€6-7)
meals.dinner: Lagos — Restaurante Casinha do Petisco — petiscos (tapas) and local wine (~€10-12)

day_by_day.notes: Check bus times carefully for the Aljezur route — services can be limited on weekdays. The Costa Vicentina is one of the last undeveloped coastlines in Western Europe and is strikingly beautiful. Bring a windbreaker as the Atlantic coast can be breezy.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed morning in Lagos. Visit the Mercado Municipal de Lagos (covered market) for fresh local produce. Take a free self-guided walking tour of Lagos's historic center — the old city walls, Porta de São Gonçalo, the 18th-century Igreja de Santa Maria, and the charming Praça da República.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Meia Praia for a final long afternoon beach session. This 4km-long beach is easily reached by a short ferry from the marina (~€1 each way) or a 15-min walk. Rent a paddleboard or simply relax. The beach is calmer and less crowded than the cliff beaches.
day_by_day.evening: Cooking experience — buy fresh ingredients from the market and use the hostel kitchen to prepare a simple Portuguese meal (bacalhau com batatas, or grilled sardines with salad). This is a great budget option and a fun social activity with other hostel guests.

meals.breakfast: Market fresh pastries and coffee (~€3)
meals.lunch: Beach snack bar at Meia Praia — grilled chicken wrap or sandwich (~€6-7)
meals.dinner: Self-cooked hostel meal — fresh ingredients from the market (~€5-7 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The small ferry across the Lagos estuary to Meia Praia is a lovely experience and very cheap. The hostel kitchen is a great resource for budget travelers — cooking even one meal per day can significantly reduce costs. Check hostel kitchen availability and rules.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Silves — the ancient Moorish capital of the Algarve. Take the train from Lagos to Tunes, then change for Silves (~€4-5 total, ~1 hour). Visit the magnificent Castelo de Silves (€2.80 entry) — one of the best-preserved Moorish castles in Portugal, with stunning views over the orange groves.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Silves old town — the Gothic Sé Catedral (€1.50 entry), the Museu Arqueológico (€2), and the charming riverside area along the Arade River. Browse the local shops for Algarve ceramics and cork products (great budget souvenirs). Visit a local wine shop — Silves is surrounded by vineyards.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos by train. Friday evening — enjoy the lively atmosphere of Lagos old town. Visit a local cervejaria (beer hall) for a final Friday night out with new hostel friends.

meals.breakfast: Lagos café before departure — coffee + pastel de nata (~€2)
meals.lunch: Silves — Restaurante Marisqueira Rui (famous for affordable cataplana) or a local café — prato do dia (~€8-10)
meals.dinner: Lagos cervejaria — imperial (draft beer) + bifanas or petiscos (~€8-10)

day_by_day.notes: Silves is a wonderful contrast to the beach-focused Algarve — rich in history and culture. The castle is particularly impressive at golden hour. The train journey through the Algarve interior passes through beautiful orange and almond groves.

day_by_day.morning: Final full beach day — revisit your favorite beach or explore Praia de Burgau, a small, authentic fishing village beach about 12km west of Lagos (bus ~€2 or bicycle). Burgau has retained its traditional character with colorful fishing boats on the beach. Swim, snorkel, and relax.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Lagos for a final afternoon of souvenir shopping and exploration. Visit the local artisan market or shops for cork products, local honey, ginjinha (cherry liqueur), and Algarve wine to take home. Pack your bags and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Lagos — splurge slightly on your last night. Visit a well-regarded local restaurant for a proper Portuguese seafood dinner. Toast to a wonderful Algarve trip with a bottle of local Algarve wine.

meals.breakfast: Hostel breakfast or local café — full Portuguese breakfast (~€4-5)
meals.lunch: Burgau beach café — fresh grilled fish of the day with salad and local wine (~€10-12)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Dom Sebastião or similar Lagos institution — grilled sea bass or cataplana for two, with local wine (~€15-18 per person — a worthy splurge on the last night)

day_by_day.notes: Burgau is a lovely, quieter alternative to the busier Lagos beaches and gives a glimpse of traditional Algarve fishing village life. For souvenirs, cork products are uniquely Portuguese, lightweight, and affordable (~€3-15). Local wine makes an excellent gift.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Lagos — enjoy a slow breakfast and a last walk through the old town. Visit the waterfront one more time for a final view of the Lagos bay. Check out of the hostel (store luggage if needed). Take a final stroll to Ponta da Piedade if time allows for a last look at those iconic cliffs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight time, take the bus or coach from Lagos to Faro Airport (Eva Bus/Rede Expressos, ~€5-7, ~1.5 hours). Allow at least 2.5-3 hours before your flight for the journey and airport check-in. Enjoy a final pastel de nata and coffee at Faro Airport.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Faro Airport. Reflect on 13 wonderful days exploring the Algarve's stunning beaches, dramatic cliffs, historic towns, and delicious wines — all on a budget!

meals.breakfast: Final Lagos café breakfast — galão + pastel de nata + tosta mista (~€4)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Lagos bus station café or pack snacks for the journey (~€4-5)
meals.dinner: Airport café or bring snacks from Lagos for the flight

day_by_day.notes: Check the bus schedule from Lagos to Faro Airport carefully — Sunday services may be less frequent. Book your return bus ticket in advance if possible. Keep some euros for airport coffee and any last-minute purchases. Total estimated budget for 13 days (excluding flights): accommodation ~€15-25/night at hostel = ~€195-325; food ~€20-25/day = ~€260-325; transport ~€5-10/day = ~€65-130; activities ~€3-10/day = ~€39-130. Grand total estimate: ~€560-910 for 13 days.

trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late night arrival
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Faro Airport at 22:30. Take the airport shuttle or pre-booked taxi (~1 hour) to Boutique Taghostel in Lagos. Check in, freshen up, and get settled.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in transit
meals.lunch: N/A — in transit
meals.dinner: Grab a late-night snack at a nearby 24-hour café or convenience store near the hostel, or pick up something light at the airport before departure.

day_by_day.notes: Flight lands at 22:30. Pre-book a taxi or arrange an airport transfer in advance to avoid delays. The drive from Faro to Lagos is approximately 70 km (about 1 hour). Keep Day 1 light — rest is the priority.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After a leisurely wake-up, take a slow morning stroll along Lagos town center. Explore the charming cobblestone streets, visit the Igreja de Santo António, and get oriented with your surroundings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Meia Praia, a long golden sandy beach just east of Lagos, easily reachable by a short taxi or bike ride. Spend the afternoon swimming, sunbathing, and relaxing — a perfect gentle introduction to the Algarve coast.
day_by_day.evening: Wander through Lagos old town at dusk. Explore the waterfront promenade (Avenida dos Descobrimentos) and enjoy the lively atmosphere as the town comes alive after sunset.

meals.breakfast: Café Ginginha or a local pastelaria near the hostel — enjoy a galão (milky coffee) and pastel de nata (custard tart) for a classic Portuguese start.
meals.lunch: O Camilo Restaurant near Lagos beach — try grilled fish of the day with salad and local bread. Mid-range, excellent quality.
meals.dinner: Restaurante Adega da Marina in Lagos — a beloved local spot serving traditional Algarvian dishes like grilled sea bass and cataplana. Budget around €20–30 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Day 2 is intentionally relaxed to allow jet lag recovery. Lagos is very walkable — pick up a free map at the hostel reception. September weather in the Algarve is typically warm (24–28°C) with minimal rain — ideal beach conditions.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Ponta da Piedade, Lagos's most iconic landmark — a dramatic series of golden limestone rock formations, arches, and sea stacks just 2 km south of the hostel. Arrive early (before 9:30 AM) to beat the crowds. Walk the clifftop trails and take in the panoramic views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a kayak or join a small boat tour from Lagos Marina to explore the sea caves and grottos beneath Ponta da Piedade up close. Tours typically last 1–1.5 hours and cost €15–25 per person.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos town for a relaxed evening. Browse the artisan shops along Rua 25 de Abril and enjoy a sundowner drink at a rooftop bar.

meals.breakfast: Pastelaria Mota near the hostel — fresh pastries, toast with local honey, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch from the Lagos Municipal Market (Mercado Municipal de Lagos) — pick up local cheeses, cured meats, fresh fruit, and bread for a cliffside picnic near Ponta da Piedade.
meals.dinner: Casinha do Petisco in Lagos — a cozy tapas-style restaurant with excellent local wines and small plates. Great for sampling multiple Algarvian flavors. Budget €20–28 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Ponta da Piedade is a 20–30 minute walk from the hostel or a short taxi ride. Wear sturdy shoes for the clifftop paths. Bring sunscreen and water. The boat/kayak tours depart from the small beach below the cliffs or from Lagos Marina.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day experience: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim. Depart Lagos by rental car or organized tour (about 35 km east). Begin the famous Seven Hanging Valleys Trail (Percurso dos Sete Vales Suspensos) — a stunning 5.7 km clifftop hike between Praia da Marinha and Praia de Vale Covo, passing dramatic arches, sea stacks, and hidden coves.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend to Praia da Marinha itself — consistently rated one of Europe's most beautiful beaches. Swim in the crystal-clear turquoise waters, explore the limestone sea caves at low tide, and relax on the sheltered golden sand.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back to Lagos. Freshen up at the hostel and enjoy a quiet evening in town.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hostel or a nearby café before departure — toast, eggs, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Pack a lunch or stop at the small beach café at Praia da Marinha for sandwiches, salads, and cold drinks.
meals.dinner: Restaurante Bon Bock in Lagos — a friendly mid-range restaurant with excellent grilled meats and fish. Try the espetada (meat skewer) or grilled dourada. Budget €18–25 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Praia da Marinha is approximately 35 km from Lagos (about 35 minutes by car). Renting a car for this day is recommended — available from €30–45/day from Lagos agencies. The hike is moderate difficulty; wear comfortable walking shoes and bring 1.5L of water per person. Check tide times — low tide is best for cave exploration.

day_by_day.morning: Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour. Drive or join a guided tour to Benagil Beach (approximately 40 km east of Lagos). Join a guided kayak tour departing from Benagil Beach to paddle through the world-famous Benagil Cave — a cathedral-like sea cave with a natural skylight opening. Tours typically last 2–3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the kayak tour, relax on Praia de Benagil or nearby Praia de Carvalho — a secluded gem accessible through a short tunnel in the cliffs. Swim and unwind after the morning's paddling.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos. Enjoy a leisurely evening walk along the marina and waterfront.

meals.breakfast: Café near the hostel — light breakfast before the active morning.
meals.lunch: Restaurante Benagil near the beach — fresh grilled fish, seafood rice, and local wine with a sea view. Budget €20–28 per person.
meals.dinner: No Pátio Restaurant in Lagos — a charming courtyard restaurant serving modern Portuguese cuisine. Try the bacalhau (salt cod) dishes. Budget €22–30 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Benagil Kayak Tour in advance — it's one of the most popular experiences in the Algarve and fills up quickly, especially in September. Tours cost approximately €35–50 per person. Bring a waterproof bag for your phone and valuables. The cave can only be entered by kayak, paddleboard, or swimming — boat tours circle outside.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Sagres and Cabo de São Vicente — the southwestern tip of continental Europe. Drive 30 km west of Lagos to Sagres. Visit the impressive Fortaleza de Sagres (Sagres Fortress), a 15th-century fortress perched dramatically on the cliffs where Henry the Navigator planned his voyages of discovery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue 6 km to Cabo de São Vicente — the most southwesterly point of mainland Europe. Stand at the edge of the continent with sweeping Atlantic views. Explore the lighthouse and browse the small artisan market. Return to Lagos via the scenic coastal road.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at the hostel's common area, meet fellow travelers, and plan the upcoming wine-focused days.

meals.breakfast: Hostel breakfast or a quick café stop in Lagos before departure.
meals.lunch: A Tasca do Sagres in Sagres village — a rustic local restaurant with excellent fresh fish soup, grilled sardines, and regional bread. Very affordable and authentic. Budget €12–18 per person.
meals.dinner: Restaurante Mullens in Lagos — a long-standing favorite with a warm atmosphere, serving traditional Portuguese dishes and a good selection of Algarve wines. Budget €20–28 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Sagres is about 30 km west of Lagos (30–35 minutes by car). The area can be windy even in September — bring a light jacket. Cabo de São Vicente is particularly dramatic at sunset if you time your visit accordingly. The drive along the Costa Vicentina is scenic and worth taking slowly.

day_by_day.morning: Algarve Wine & Cataplana Tasting Experience. Drive to the Lagoa wine region (approximately 45 km east of Lagos). Visit a local winery — such as Adega do Cantor or Quinta dos Vales — for a guided tour of the vineyards and wine cellar, learning about the unique Algarve terroir and indigenous grape varieties like Negra Mole and Crato Branco.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the tasting experience with a traditional Cataplana cooking demonstration and lunch pairing. The cataplana (a copper clam-shaped cooking vessel) is the iconic dish of the Algarve — typically made with clams, pork, or fish with local spices. Pair with regional white and red wines.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos in the late afternoon. Enjoy a quiet evening strolling the old town.

meals.breakfast: Café stop in Lagos before departure — coffee and pastries.
meals.lunch: Included as part of the Algarve Wine & Cataplana Tasting Experience at the winery — a full paired lunch with multiple wine pours.
meals.dinner: Restaurante O Camilo in Lagos — a cliffside restaurant with spectacular views and excellent fresh seafood. Try the grilled lobster or seafood cataplana. Budget €25–35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Algarve Wine & Cataplana Tasting Experience typically costs €55–80 per person including the winery tour, tasting, and paired lunch. Book in advance. Designate a driver or arrange a taxi/tour transfer if you plan to taste wines fully. The Lagoa wine region is the most productive wine area in the Algarve.

day_by_day.morning: Silves Castle & Old Town Food Walk. Drive to Silves (approximately 35 km northeast of Lagos). Begin with a visit to the magnificent Castelo de Silves — a well-preserved Moorish red sandstone castle dating from the 8th century, offering panoramic views over the orange groves and Arade River valley.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join the guided Old Town Food Walk through Silves' historic streets. Sample local specialties including medronho (arbutus berry brandy), local cheeses, almond sweets, smoked sausages, and traditional pastries at artisan shops and local producers. The walk covers the cathedral, the old Moorish quarter, and the riverside.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos. Enjoy a relaxed evening with a glass of wine at a Lagos wine bar.

meals.breakfast: Café in Lagos before departure.
meals.lunch: Included in the Silves Food Walk — multiple tastings throughout the old town constitute a full lunch experience.
meals.dinner: Vinha Bar in Lagos — a cozy wine bar with an excellent selection of Portuguese wines by the glass and a tapas menu featuring local charcuterie, cheeses, and small plates. Budget €18–25 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Silves is approximately 35 km from Lagos (about 40 minutes by car). The Silves Castle & Old Town Food Walk typically costs €35–55 per person. The castle entrance fee is approximately €3. September is harvest season in the Algarve — you may see orange and almond harvests in progress around Silves, adding to the experience.

day_by_day.morning: Beach day at Praia de Dona Ana — one of Lagos's most beautiful and accessible beaches, just 2 km from the hostel. Arrive early to secure a good spot. The beach is framed by dramatic ochre cliffs and has calm, clear water ideal for swimming and snorkeling.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a stand-up paddleboard or take a snorkeling excursion from Praia de Dona Ana. Explore the underwater rock formations and colorful marine life. Alternatively, simply relax on the beach and read.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks at a clifftop bar above Praia de Dona Ana, then dinner in Lagos.

meals.breakfast: Café Atlântico in Lagos — a popular local breakfast spot with fresh juices, eggs, and pastries.
meals.lunch: Beach restaurant at Praia de Dona Ana — grilled fish, salads, and cold drinks with your feet in the sand. Budget €15–22 per person.
meals.dinner: Restaurante Laranjeira in Lagos — a charming mid-range restaurant in the old town with excellent traditional Portuguese cuisine and a good wine list. Budget €20–28 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Praia de Dona Ana is a 20–25 minute walk from the hostel or a short taxi ride. It can get busy in September — arrive before 10 AM for the best spots. The cliffs provide some natural shade in the late afternoon. SUP and snorkel rentals are available on the beach for approximately €15–20/hour.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Tavira — one of the most beautiful and authentic towns in the Algarve, approximately 110 km east of Lagos. Explore the charming town center with its Roman bridge, whitewashed churches, and Moorish-influenced architecture. Visit the Castelo de Tavira for panoramic views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the ferry from Tavira to Ilha de Tavira — a stunning barrier island beach with pristine white sand and calm, shallow waters. Spend the afternoon swimming and relaxing on one of the Algarve's most beautiful and unspoiled beaches.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos by car or bus. Enjoy a quiet dinner near the hostel.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hostel before the drive.
meals.lunch: Restaurante Bica in Tavira — a beloved local institution serving excellent fresh fish and seafood at very reasonable prices. Try the grilled bream or seafood rice. Budget €15–22 per person.
meals.dinner: Tasca do Zé in Lagos — a small, unpretentious local tasca (tavern) with daily specials, excellent value, and a very local atmosphere. Budget €12–18 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Tavira is approximately 110 km east of Lagos (about 1 hour 15 minutes by car). Alternatively, take the train from Lagos to Tavira (about 1.5–2 hours, €8–12 each way) for a scenic and relaxing journey. The ferry to Ilha de Tavira runs frequently and costs approximately €2 each way. Bring cash for the ferry.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the western Algarve's wild coast — drive north from Lagos along the Costa Vicentina to Aljezur and the Parque Natural do Sudoeste Alentejano e Costa Vicentina. Visit Praia da Arrifana — a dramatic surf beach backed by towering cliffs, popular with surfers and nature lovers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Praia de Monte Clérigo or Praia da Amoreira — wild, windswept Atlantic beaches with a completely different character from the sheltered southern Algarve beaches. Walk the clifftop paths and enjoy the raw natural beauty.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos. Visit a local wine shop to pick up a bottle of Algarve wine to enjoy at the hostel's terrace.

meals.breakfast: Café stop in Aljezur village — a charming hilltop town with good local cafés.
meals.lunch: Restaurante Arrifana near the beach — fresh fish and seafood with Atlantic views. Budget €18–25 per person.
meals.dinner: Self-catered evening at the hostel — pick up local bread, cheese, charcuterie, olives, and a bottle of Algarve wine from a local supermarket or deli. Enjoy on the hostel terrace. Budget €10–15 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Costa Vicentina is part of a protected natural park — one of the last undeveloped coastlines in Western Europe. The beaches here are wilder and more exposed than the southern Algarve. Water temperatures are cooler on the Atlantic-facing west coast. Aljezur is approximately 35 km north of Lagos (about 40 minutes by car).

day_by_day.morning: Return visit to a favorite Lagos beach for a final morning swim — choose Praia do Camilo, a small and intimate beach just south of Lagos accessible via a wooden staircase down the cliffs. Arrive early for the best experience before day-trippers arrive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Afternoon wine tasting at a Lagos wine bar or visit the local Adega Cooperativa de Lagos — the local wine cooperative where you can taste and purchase bottles of authentic Algarve wines directly from the producer at excellent prices.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Lagos — celebrate the end of the trip with a special meal at one of Lagos's best restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at a favorite Lagos café — treat yourself to a full Portuguese breakfast with eggs, presunto (cured ham), local cheese, and fresh orange juice.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a beachside café near Praia do Camilo — sandwiches, salads, and cold drinks.
meals.dinner: Restaurante Dom Sebastião in Lagos — one of the finest traditional restaurants in Lagos, known for its exceptional cataplana, grilled fish, and extensive Portuguese wine list. A fitting farewell dinner. Budget €30–45 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Praia do Camilo is a 25-minute walk from the hostel or a short taxi ride. The wooden staircase down to the beach is steep — wear appropriate footwear. The Adega Cooperativa de Lagos is located just outside the town center and offers excellent value wines — stock up on bottles to take home. Check airline liquid restrictions for packing wine.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Lagos — wake up early for one last walk through the old town. Visit the Mercado Municipal de Lagos for fresh produce, local honey, almond products, and artisan goods as final souvenirs. Stroll along the city walls and enjoy a last coffee at a favorite café.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the hostel (standard checkout is 11 AM — arrange late checkout if needed). Pack and prepare for departure. If time allows before transfer, visit the Museu Municipal de Lagos for a fascinating overview of the region's history from prehistoric times through the Age of Discovery.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer to Faro Airport for departure. Allow at least 2 hours before your flight for the journey and check-in.

meals.breakfast: Final pastel de nata and galão at a Lagos pastelaria — a perfect last taste of Portugal.
meals.lunch: Light lunch near the hostel or at the airport — keep it simple on departure day.
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight meal depending on departure time.

day_by_day.notes: Check out time at Boutique Taghostel is typically 11 AM — confirm with reception and arrange luggage storage if needed for a late afternoon departure. The drive from Lagos to Faro Airport is approximately 70 km (about 1 hour). Pre-book your return transfer in advance. Faro Airport has limited dining options — eat in Lagos before heading to the airport if possible.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Portugal Algarve Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Boutique Taghostel
hotel.location: Rua Dr. Faria e Silva, 32, Lagos, PT (37.1038,-8.6730)

experiences.name: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim
experiences.description: Explore one of the Algarve's most stunning beaches, known for its dramatic limestone cliffs, sea caves, and crystal-clear turquoise waters. Hike the clifftop trail from Benagil and descend to the secluded cove for a refreshing swim.

experiences.name: Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour
experiences.description: Paddle through the iconic Benagil Cave, one of the world's most beautiful sea caves, accessible only by water. A guided kayak tour takes you through hidden grottos and arches along the golden coastline, offering a unique perspective of the Algarve's dramatic geology.

experiences.name: Algarve Wine & Cataplana Tasting Experience
experiences.description: Visit a local winery in the Lagoa wine region, the heart of Algarve viticulture, for a guided tasting of regional wines including Arinto and Negra Mole varieties. Pair your wines with a traditional Cataplana seafood stew prepared by a local chef.

experiences.name: Ria Formosa Natural Park Boat Tour
experiences.description: Cruise through the stunning Ria Formosa lagoon system, a protected natural park spanning 60km of coastline. Discover barrier islands, flamingo colonies, and secluded barrier beaches only accessible by boat, with stops for swimming and snorkeling in calm lagoon waters.

experiences.name: Silves Castle & Old Town Food Walk
experiences.description: Explore the Moorish red sandstone castle of Silves, the ancient Algarve capital, followed by a guided food walk through the historic old town. Sample local specialties including carob products, medronho brandy, almond sweets, and fresh orange juice at traditional market stalls.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Arrival day
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - Arrival day
day_by_day.evening: Late arrival at Faro Airport at 22:30. Private luxury transfer arranged to Boutique Taghostel in Lagos (~1 hour drive). Check-in, unwind with a welcome glass of local Algarve wine left by the hotel, and settle into your premium suite.

meals.breakfast: N/A
meals.lunch: N/A
meals.dinner: Light late-night charcuterie and cheese board with Portuguese wine arranged by the hotel upon arrival request.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange private airport transfer with a luxury car service (e.g., Mercedes E-Class or similar). Confirm late check-in with Boutique Taghostel in advance. Keep Day 1 light — rest is the priority.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely start with a gourmet breakfast at the hotel. Afterwards, take a relaxed orientation walk through Lagos Old Town — explore the historic city walls, Praça Gil Eanes, and the charming cobblestone streets. Visit the Igreja de Santo António, a stunning baroque church.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Meia Praia, Lagos's longest and most accessible premium beach (10 min from hotel). Rent a private sun lounger and parasol setup. Enjoy the calm Atlantic waters and golden sands. Optional: book a private paddleboard or kayak rental directly on the beach.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Restaurante Adega da Marina in Lagos — a beloved upscale local institution known for fresh grilled fish, cataplana dishes, and an excellent Portuguese wine list. Stroll along the Lagos marina waterfront after dinner.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at Boutique Taghostel — fresh pastries, local cheeses, cured meats, fresh fruit, and specialty coffee.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a beachside chiringuito at Meia Praia — grilled prawns, fresh salads, and chilled Vinho Verde.
meals.dinner: Restaurante Adega da Marina — grilled sea bass, cataplana de marisco, and a bottle of Algarve Lagoa white wine.

day_by_day.notes: This is a gentle acclimatization day after the late arrival. Lagos Old Town is walkable from the hotel. Meia Praia is a 10-minute taxi or Uber ride.

day_by_day.morning: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim — depart early for this iconic guided coastal hike along the dramatic limestone cliffs between Praia da Marinha and Benagil. Marvel at sea arches, grottos, and turquoise coves. The guide will lead you to hidden swimming spots accessible only on foot.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the hike, spend the afternoon relaxing and swimming at Praia da Marinha itself — consistently rated one of Europe's most beautiful beaches. Rent a private lounger setup and enjoy the crystal-clear waters surrounded by golden cliffs.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward Lagos and dine at Vila Joya Bistro in Albufeira (30 min from Lagos) — a Michelin-starred experience offering contemporary Portuguese cuisine with stunning ocean views.

meals.breakfast: Early gourmet breakfast at the hotel before departure.
meals.lunch: Packed premium picnic lunch arranged by the hotel, or dine at the charming Restaurante Marinha in Carvoeiro near the beach — fresh seafood platters and local wines.
meals.dinner: Vila Joya Bistro — tasting menu with wine pairing featuring the finest Algarve and Alentejo wines. Reservation essential.

day_by_day.notes: Praia da Marinha is approximately 45 minutes east of Lagos by car. Hire a private driver for the day for maximum comfort. Wear comfortable hiking shoes and bring sunscreen, a hat, and water. Book Vila Joya well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour — depart from Praia de Benagil for a guided kayak tour through the world-famous Benagil Cave. Paddle through sea arches, hidden grottoes, and emerald waters. The tour includes stops at secluded beaches accessible only by sea.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the kayak tour, relax at Praia de Benagil or nearby Praia do Carvalho — a hidden gem accessible via a short tunnel through the cliffs. Swim, sunbathe, and enjoy the dramatic scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos and enjoy a sunset cocktail at the rooftop bar of a Lagos hotel (e.g., Hotel Tivoli Lagos rooftop) overlooking the bay. Dinner at O Camilo restaurant perched dramatically above Praia do Camilo — exceptional fresh seafood with cliff-top views.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the hotel.
meals.lunch: Post-kayak lunch at Restaurante Benagil — grilled fish of the day, local bread, and chilled rosé.
meals.dinner: O Camilo, Lagos — grilled lobster, percebes (barnacles), and a premium Algarve white wine selection.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Benagil Kayak Tour in advance as spots fill quickly, especially in September. Wear a swimsuit under clothes and bring a dry bag for valuables. The kayak tour typically lasts 2–3 hours.

day_by_day.morning: Algarve Wine & Cataplana Tasting Experience — private transfer to the Lagoa wine region (30 min east of Lagos), the heart of Algarve viticulture. Enjoy a guided winery tour learning about the unique terroir of the Algarve, followed by a structured tasting of premium Algarve wines including Negra Mole and Crato Branco varietals.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the experience with a traditional Cataplana cooking demonstration and tasting lunch at the winery — the iconic copper pot dish filled with clams, prawns, and chorizo, paired with estate wines. Explore the vineyard grounds and olive groves.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos for a relaxed evening. Stroll through the Mercado de Lagos (if open) or browse the boutique shops in the old town. Dinner at Restaurante Casinha do Petisco — an intimate, upscale local restaurant known for creative Portuguese tapas and natural wines.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the hotel.
meals.lunch: Cataplana tasting lunch at the winery — included in the experience.
meals.dinner: Casinha do Petisco, Lagos — petiscos (Portuguese tapas), octopus carpaccio, and a curated natural wine selection.

day_by_day.notes: The Algarve Wine & Cataplana Tasting Experience is a full half-day activity. Arrange private transport to and from the Lagoa wine region. Consider purchasing a few bottles of estate wine to enjoy during the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Sagres and Cabo de São Vicente — the southwestern-most point of continental Europe. Visit the dramatic Fortaleza de Sagres, a 15th-century fortress with sweeping Atlantic views. Walk the clifftop paths and watch the waves crash against the ancient rocks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the beaches around Sagres — Praia do Martinhal is a premium, sheltered beach ideal for swimming and water sports. Rent a private cabana setup and enjoy the uncrowded, pristine sands. Optional: book a private surf lesson with a premium surf school.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Restaurante Memmo Baleeira in Sagres — a sophisticated restaurant at the boutique Memmo Baleeira Hotel with panoramic ocean views, serving creative modern Portuguese cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the hotel.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a Sagres beachside café — fresh tuna steak, local bread, and a glass of chilled Alentejo white.
meals.dinner: Memmo Baleeira Restaurant, Sagres — tasting menu with Atlantic-inspired dishes and premium wine pairing.

day_by_day.notes: Sagres is approximately 30 minutes west of Lagos. Hire a private driver for the day. Cabo de São Vicente is particularly spectacular at sunset — time your visit accordingly. Book Memmo Baleeira dinner in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed morning at leisure — sleep in, enjoy a long breakfast, and spend time at the hotel. Optional: book an in-hotel spa treatment or a private yoga session arranged through the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Praia Dona Ana — one of Lagos's most iconic and photogenic beaches, just 15 minutes from the hotel. Rent a private boat or RIB for a 2-hour private coastal cruise along the Lagos grottos and sea caves, including Ponta da Piedade — the most spectacular rock formation in the Algarve.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at Ponta da Piedade viewpoint (if not seen from the boat). Dinner at Restaurante Eleven in Lagos — a premium fine dining experience with a focus on seasonal Portuguese ingredients and an award-winning wine cellar.

meals.breakfast: Extended gourmet breakfast at the hotel — treat yourself to the full spread.
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch at Praia Dona Ana beach restaurant — grilled sea bream, salad, and chilled rosé.
meals.dinner: Restaurante Eleven, Lagos — chef's tasting menu with Algarve and Douro wine pairing.

day_by_day.notes: Private boat hire for the Ponta da Piedade coastal cruise can be arranged through the hotel concierge. This is a mid-trip rest day — pace yourself for the second week.

day_by_day.morning: Silves Castle & Old Town Food Walk — private transfer to Silves (45 min from Lagos), the ancient Moorish capital of the Algarve. Begin with a guided tour of the magnificent red sandstone Castelo de Silves, exploring its towers, cisterns, and panoramic views over the orange groves.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the guided food walk through Silves Old Town — taste local specialties including medronho (arbutus berry spirit), almond sweets, smoked sausages, local cheeses, and traditional pastries at artisan shops and market stalls. Visit the Silves Cathedral and the Roman bridge.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Restaurante Marisqueira Rui in Silves — a legendary seafood institution beloved by locals and food critics alike, known for its exceptional fresh shellfish and cataplana dishes.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the hotel before departure.
meals.lunch: Included tastings during the Silves food walk — a progressive lunch of local specialties.
meals.dinner: Marisqueira Rui, Silves — cataplana de lingueirão (razor clams), grilled tiger prawns, and a bottle of Algarve Lagoa white wine.

day_by_day.notes: Silves is approximately 45 minutes northeast of Lagos. Arrange private transport. The Silves Medieval Castle Festival may be running in early September — check dates. Book Marisqueira Rui in advance as it is very popular.

day_by_day.morning: Ria Formosa Natural Park Boat Tour — private transfer to Faro (1.5 hours east of Lagos). Board a premium private boat for a guided tour of the Ria Formosa lagoon system — a UNESCO-protected natural park. Cruise through tidal channels, visit barrier islands, and spot flamingos, herons, and other migratory birds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Disembark at Ilha Deserta (Desert Island) — the most remote and pristine barrier island in Ria Formosa. Spend the afternoon on this car-free, unspoiled beach with crystal-clear lagoon waters. Lunch at the island's only restaurant, Estaminé, a renowned seafood destination.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Faro by boat and explore the charming Faro Old Town (Cidade Velha) — the walled historic center with its cathedral, Roman walls, and atmospheric squares. Private transfer back to Lagos. Light dinner in Lagos.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the hotel before early departure.
meals.lunch: Estaminé Restaurant, Ilha Deserta — fresh oysters, grilled fish, and chilled Vinho Verde in a stunning natural setting.
meals.dinner: Restaurante Adega da Marina, Lagos — lighter dinner of grilled fish and local wine after a full day.

day_by_day.notes: This is a long day trip — depart Lagos by 8:00 AM. Arrange a private luxury transfer to Faro. Book the private Ria Formosa boat tour in advance. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and a light layer for the boat.

day_by_day.morning: Private wine tasting and vineyard tour at Quinta dos Vales — one of the Algarve's most acclaimed premium wineries near Estômbar (40 min from Lagos). Enjoy a private guided tour of the estate, sculpture garden, and wine cellar, followed by a premium tasting of their award-winning red, white, and rosé wines.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the winery, visit the nearby Carvoeiro village — a picturesque fishing village with a stunning beach cove. Explore the Algar Seco rock formations (dramatic coastal rock formations accessible by boardwalk) and relax at Praia de Carvoeiro.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Restaurante Bon Bon in Carvoeiro — a Michelin-starred restaurant offering an extraordinary tasting menu of creative modern Portuguese cuisine with exceptional wine pairings.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the hotel.
meals.lunch: Premium wine and cheese pairing lunch at Quinta dos Vales — included in the private winery experience.
meals.dinner: Restaurante Bon Bon, Carvoeiro — Michelin-starred tasting menu with full wine pairing. Reservation essential and must be booked well in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Quinta dos Vales offers private tours — book directly with the estate. Restaurante Bon Bon is one of the Algarve's most sought-after reservations — book as early as possible, ideally months in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Monchique — the lush mountain village in the Serra de Monchique (1 hour from Lagos). Hike or drive to the summit of Fóia, the highest point in the Algarve (902m), for panoramic views stretching to the Atlantic. Explore the charming village streets and visit the Convento de Nossa Senhora do Desterro ruins.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Monchique thermal spa town of Caldas de Monchique — a historic spa resort nestled in a wooded valley. Enjoy a premium spa treatment at the Termas de Monchique wellness center, famous for its bicarbonated mineral waters. Browse the artisan shops for local medronho, honey, and smoked sausages.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos for a final evening in the western Algarve. Sunset cocktails at a Lagos rooftop bar. Farewell dinner at Restaurante Casinha do Petisco or a new discovery in Lagos old town.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the hotel.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Restaurante Central in Monchique — traditional mountain cuisine including roast kid (cabrito), black pork, and local wines.
meals.dinner: Restaurante O Camilo, Lagos — final dinner with cliff-top views, grilled lobster, and a premium Algarve wine selection.

day_by_day.notes: Monchique offers a completely different landscape from the coast — lush eucalyptus and cork oak forests. Hire a private driver for the mountain roads. Book the Termas de Monchique spa treatment in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Final beach morning — return to your favorite beach from the trip (Praia da Marinha, Praia Dona Ana, or Meia Praia) for a last swim in the Atlantic. Rent a premium lounger setup and soak in the September sunshine and warm sea temperatures.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Lagos for a leisurely afternoon. Visit the Mercado de Lagos for last-minute local souvenirs — local wines, almond products, artisan ceramics, and cork goods. Enjoy a final stroll through the old town and along the marina.
day_by_day.evening: Premium farewell dinner at Restaurante Eleven or Vila Joya Bistro — a celebratory final meal with a special wine pairing to mark the end of the trip. After dinner, enjoy a nightcap at a Lagos wine bar.

meals.breakfast: Extended gourmet breakfast at the hotel — savor every last bite.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a Lagos old town café — petiscos, local cheese, and a glass of chilled Algarve rosé.
meals.dinner: Grand farewell dinner — chef's tasting menu with premium Algarve and Douro wine pairing at your chosen Michelin-level restaurant.

day_by_day.notes: Pack bags this evening for an early departure the following morning. Confirm private airport transfer for Day 13. Purchase any remaining wine or local products to take home.

day_by_day.morning: Final gourmet breakfast at Boutique Taghostel. Check out of the hotel. Private luxury transfer to Faro Airport for departure flight. Arrive at the airport with ample time for a relaxed departure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Departure from Faro Airport. If flight is in the afternoon, enjoy the airport lounges or spend extra time in Faro Old Town before heading to the airport.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — carry the memories of 13 extraordinary days in the Algarve.

meals.breakfast: Final gourmet breakfast at the hotel before checkout.
meals.lunch: Airport lounge or a final coffee and pastel de nata at a Faro café near the airport.
meals.dinner: In-flight or at destination.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private luxury transfer from Lagos to Faro Airport (approximately 1 hour). Allow at least 2.5 hours before departure for check-in and security. Consider purchasing a case of Algarve wines to ship home or check as luggage.
